title: Genetic exploration of Dravet syndrome: two case report.
ehr_evidence: The study did not use electronic health records; genetic analysis was performed on biospecimens via whole-genome sequencing, whole-exome sequencing, and Sanger sequencing at 3Billion (Seoul, Korea).
summary: A case series of two Indonesian (Javanese) pediatric patients with Dravet syndrome who underwent next-generation sequencing to identify causative genetic variants and correlate mutations with clinical severity.
key_findings: Patient 1 (aged 11 years 2 months) had a heterozygous pathogenic 552.9 Kb deletion at 2q24.3 spanning TTC21B, SCN1A, and SCN9A genes.
Patient 2 (aged 1 year 4 months) had a novel likely pathogenic heterozygous splice-site mutation in SCN1A (c.4003-2A>G, upstream of exon 24).
The more severe the genetic mutation detected, the more severe the clinical manifestations; patient 1 (three-gene mutation) had worse seizure control than patient 2 (single SCN1A mutation).
Inheritance patterns were unresolved in both cases due to inability to perform parental Sanger sequencing.
Removing contraindicated sodium-channel blockers (oxcarbazepine in patient 1, phenytoin in patient 2) improved seizure control in both patients.
population: Two Indonesian (Javanese) children at a tertiary referral hospital in Indonesia: a boy aged 11 years 2 months and a girl aged 1 year 4 months, both with Dravet syndrome.
exposure_domain: none (genetic study; no environmental exposure analyzed)
limitations: Only two cases were analyzed, limiting generalizability.
Inheritance patterns remained unresolved because parental Sanger sequencing could not be performed.
No environmental or exposome data were collected.
